title: Jeremiah Bible Quiz - Chapter 30
description: Ten questions on Jeremiah 30: the words written in a book, the time of Jacob's trouble, and the promise of healing for Zion.

questions.text: What was Jeremiah told to do with all the words Yahweh had spoken to him?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said, "Write all the words that I have spoken to you in a book."

answers.text: Read them in the court of the temple
Send them to the king of Babylon
Write them in a book
Keep them to himself

questions.text: What did Yahweh say He would do for His people Israel and Judah?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said the days come that He will reverse the captivity of his people Israel and Judah, and cause them to return to the land He gave to their fathers, and they will possess it.

answers.text: Reverse their captivity and bring them back to the land of their fathers
Give their land away to the nations around them
Keep them among the nations for ever and ever
Make them serve the king of Babylon's son's son

questions.text: How does the text describe the men whom the speaker sees?
questions.explanation: The text asks whether a man travails with child, and says every man is seen with his hands on his waist, as a woman in travail, and all faces are turned pale.

answers.text: Singing with gladness in the height of Zion
Sleeping quietly while the storm passes by
Running to the gates with their weapons
With hands on the waist, like a woman in travail, and faces pale

questions.text: What is that great day called in verse 7?
questions.explanation: The text says, "Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it. It is even the time of Jacob's trouble; but he will be saved out of it."

answers.text: The day of the shepherds
The time of Jacob's trouble
The year of their visitation
The day of the new covenant

questions.text: What did Yahweh of Armies say He would break and burst in that day?
questions.explanation: Yahweh of Armies said He would break his yoke from off your neck and burst your bonds, and strangers would no more make them their bondservants.

answers.text: The yoke from off their neck, and their bonds
The gates of the city of Jerusalem
The vessels of Yahweh's temple
The bow and the sword of the enemy

questions.text: Whom does the text say they would serve instead?
questions.explanation: The text says they will serve Yahweh their God, and David their king, whom Yahweh will raise up to them.

answers.text: The shepherds set over them
Strangers in a far country
Yahweh their God, and David their king
The prince of the nations

questions.text: What difference did Yahweh make between the nations and His own people?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said He would make a full end of all the nations where He had scattered them, but He would not make a full end of them; He would correct them in measure.

answers.text: He would scatter the nations but gather no one
He would spare both alike
He would leave his people wholly unpunished
He would make a full end of the nations, but not of His people

questions.text: How is their hurt described in verses 12 and 13?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said, "Your hurt is incurable. Your wound is grievous," and that there was no one to plead their cause and they had no healing medicines.

answers.text: Light, and soon forgotten
Incurable and grievous, with no healing medicines
Hidden, so that no one could see it
Already bound up by their lovers

questions.text: What did Yahweh nevertheless promise to do for the one called an outcast?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said, "For I will restore health to you, and I will heal you of your wounds," because they had called her an outcast, saying, "It is Zion, whom no man seeks after."

answers.text: Restore her health and heal her wounds
Give her a new name among the nations
Send her prophets and diviners
Leave her in the hand of her adversaries

questions.text: What did Yahweh say in verse 22 about Himself and the people?
questions.explanation: Yahweh said, "You shall be my people, and I will be your God."

answers.text: That He would hide his face from them
That He would give them to other shepherds
That they would be his people and He would be their God
That He would be a God afar off only
